art_observations: The final 32px exports retain a range of fine and coarse grain, clasts, pores, fractures, horizontal bedding and diagonal foliation. Contact sheets use nearest-neighbor enlargement of the actual exported files.

No conspicuous rectangular boundary grid was found in the inspected 3x3 proofs. Repeated motifs remain visible, especially in coarse crystalline, clast-rich and banded surfaces. Passing the statistical screen is not seamlessness acceptance.

Gneiss and migmatite have strong band direction; halite, pegmatite, soapstone and volcanic agglomerate have conspicuous recurring coarse forms. Assess large native surfaces and orientation before promotion.
The 32/16/8/4px mechanical scale study shows fine crystalline detail and chalk cracks fading at small scales. Gneiss banding persists longer, then loses structure at 4px.

Coal ranks have distinct 32px structures: fibrous lignite, dull compact subbituminous fragments, banded bituminous coal and angular anthracite. Their differences weaken at 8px and are largely lost at 4px; verify low-light readability in the native renderer.
